name: torch-mlp-reproducibility
research_question: How far does a real PyTorch training run move under controlled perturbations of the thread count, the loss implementation, the model width, the dataset version and the batch size - relative to how far it moves when only the random seed changes?
hypothesis: Changing the CPU thread count perturbs floating-point reduction order and so moves the loss slightly, while leaving accuracy untouched; the model width, the dataset version and the batch size move both. Fixing the seed does not make training deterministic across thread counts.
headline: mlp scored 0.1639 +/- 0.0023 on test_loss over 10 seeds, beating every baseline; the narrowest margin is +0.5056 over logistic-regression [0.5038, 0.5075] (paired-t, adjusted p=0.0000).

claims.statement: mlp scored 0.1639 against logistic-regression's 0.6695 on test_loss (10 replications each, +0.5056 [0.5038, 0.5075] at 95% confidence). The difference is statistically detectable (paired-t, adjusted p=0.0000) with a large effect size (Hedges' g=-182.09).

interval.note: signed so that positive means better, matching the metric's direction

claims.statement: implementation (torch-mlp-unfused-loss): moved test_loss by +0.0000 [0.0000, 0.0000], 0.0x the seed noise; stability 1.00 [1.00, 1.00] (not distinguishable from relabelling noise, permutation p=1.000), within the declared tolerance of 0.02.

environment (single-threaded): moved test_loss by +0.0000 [-0.0000, 0.0001], 0.0x the seed noise; stability 1.00 [0.98, 1.00] (not distinguishable from relabelling noise, permutation p=0.858), within the declared tolerance of 0.02.

environment (two-threaded): moved test_loss by +0.0000 [-0.0000, 0.0001], 0.0x the seed noise; stability 1.00 [1.00, 1.00] (not distinguishable from relabelling noise, permutation p=0.918), within the declared tolerance of 0.02.

configuration (batch-32): moved test_loss by -0.0001 [-0.0026, 0.0024], 0.1x the seed noise; stability 1.00 [1.00, 1.00] (not distinguishable from relabelling noise, permutation p=0.930), within the declared tolerance of 0.02.
dataset (spiral@v2): moved test_loss by +0.1884 [0.1857, 0.1911], 80.5x the seed noise; stability 0.00, beyond the declared tolerance of 0.02.

model (mlp-2x128@v2): moved test_loss by -0.0008 [-0.0021, 0.0004], 0.4x the seed noise; stability 0.91 [0.70, 1.00] (not distinguishable from relabelling noise, permutation p=0.309), within the declared tolerance of 0.02.

Deterministic: 4 executions of an identical run produced identical values on every result metric (accuracy, test_loss, threads, train_loss). train_seconds varied, as expected: those measure the machine rather than the method.

limitations: With 10 replications and the observed spread, this design could detect a difference of 0.0025 in test_loss or larger 80% of the time at alpha=0.05.
Changing the dataset moves test_loss by +0.1884, beyond the declared tolerance of 0.02. Results should not be expected to reproduce across dataset changes.

reproducibility.method: stability(axis) = 1 - max(0, (|Cliff's delta| - E|delta|_null) / (1 - E|delta|_null)), where E|delta|_null is the mean |Cliff's delta| under random relabelling of the same samples. The seed axis is the reference noise floor and is not scored.

seed.description: seed: 10 seeds of 'mlp' give test_loss = 0.1639 +/- 0.0023 (CV 1.43%), mean [0.1622, 0.1656]. A replication using 5 of these seeds would reach the same conclusion 0% of the time, but that is a limit of the test rather than of the effect: with 5 runs the smallest attainable p-value is 0.0625, which is above alpha, so no 5-seed replication could reach significance whatever it measured.
seed.role: reference noise floor; not scored as a perturbation
